problem:
Consider the function $f(x,y)=-{x}^{3}(y+1).$ Fill in the missing signs in the sign table of $f(x,y)$ shown below.

| $y>-1$ | {{field-1}} | {{field-2}} |
| --- | --- | --- |
| $y<-1$ | {{field-3}} | {{field-4}} |
|  | $x<0$ | $x>0$ |

feedback.problem:
Consider the expression $f(x,y)=(x-1)^{2}(y+1).$  What are the missing entries in the sign table of $f(x,y),$ shown below?

| $y>-1$ |  |  |
| --- | --- | --- |
| $y<-1$ |  |  |
|  | $x<1$ | $x>1$ |
feedback.worked_solution:
Notice that $f(x,y)$ equals zero when $x=1$ and $y=-1.$ These lines divide the $xy$-plane into four regions, as shown below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/14037232/assets/23195f0e8657cfbd219f540d6f4403c6bffe1056849e4da43a11b61f4afba76a.png)

To determine the sign of $f(x,y)$ in each region, we pick four test points, one for each region.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/14037232/assets/fad89577df15122a8f80996cbf4f1b840084f51cd93d97a776f5562d59a4cc99.png)

Next, we calculate the sign of $f(x,y)$ in each region using a sign table:

|  | Test point | $(x-1)^{2}$ | $(y+1)$ | $f(x,y)$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Top-left | $(-2,0)$ | $+$ | $+$ | $+$ |
| Top-Right | $(4,0)$ | $+$ | $+$ | $+$ |
| Bottom-Left | $(-2,-2)$ | $+$ | $-$ | $-$ |
| Bottom-Right | $(4,-2)$ | $+$ | $-$ | $-$ |

 

Using the *last* column of the table above, we get the following picture:

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/14037232/assets/ba5f76185cc6d2e25204c10e8e25b0bf28b3686cb1d494f87af8f03c4b2f2b66.png)

Finally, we fill in the required sign table.

| $y>-1$ | $+$ | $+$ |
| --- | --- | --- |
| $y<-1$ | $-$ | $-$ |
|  | $x<1$ | $x>1$ |
